statements.text: Brazil is the only country in the Americas where Portuguese is the main language.
Brazil has won the men's football World Cup five times, more than any other country.
Brazil's capital is Rio de Janeiro.
statements.truth: Brasília has been Brazil's capital since 1960. Rio de Janeiro was the capital before that.

statements.text: In parts of northern Norway, the sun doesn't set for weeks in the middle of summer.
Norway's coast is famous for its fjords, long narrow inlets carved out by glaciers.
Norway is a member of the European Union.
statements.truth: Norwegians voted against joining in 1972 and again in 1994. Norway works closely with the EU through the European Economic Area instead.

statements.text: Kenya is named after Mount Kenya, the second-highest mountain in Africa.
The equator runs through Kenya.
Kenya's capital is Mombasa.
statements.truth: Kenya's capital is Nairobi. Mombasa is its biggest port, on the Indian Ocean coast.

statements.text: All of China officially runs on a single time zone, despite the country's huge width.
Papermaking was invented in China around 2,000 years ago.
The Great Wall of China is easy to see from the Moon with the naked eye.
statements.truth: This is a popular myth. The wall is far too narrow to see from the Moon, and it's hard to spot even from low orbit.

statements.text: Iceland has no standing army.
Iceland's parliament, the Althing, was founded in 930 and is one of the oldest in the world.
More than half of Iceland is covered by glaciers.
statements.truth: Glaciers and lakes together cover only about 14% of Iceland. Much of the rest is highland, lava fields and tundra.

statements.text: Japan is made up of more than 14,000 islands.
Japan has more than 100 active volcanoes.
Japan's national flower is the lotus.
statements.truth: Japan has no national flower set in law, but the cherry blossom and the chrysanthemum are its traditional floral symbols.

statements.text: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still largely standing.
Most Egyptians live along the Nile and its delta.
The Nile flows south through Egypt toward the Red Sea.
statements.truth: The Nile flows north through Egypt and empties into the Mediterranean Sea.

statements.text: Thailand is the only country in Southeast Asia that was never colonised by a Western power.
Bangkok's full ceremonial name is one of the longest place names in the world.
Thailand used to be called Burma.
statements.truth: Thailand was officially called Siam until 1939. Burma is the former name of neighbouring Myanmar.

statements.text: About half of the Netherlands is less than 1 m (3 ft) above sea level, and much of that is below it.
Amsterdam is the capital, but the government sits in The Hague.
Tulips are native to the Netherlands.
statements.truth: Wild tulips come from Central Asia and the region around Türkiye. They reached the Netherlands in the 1500s.

statements.text: Chile is more than 4,000 km (2,500 mi) long but on average less than 200 km (120 mi) wide.
Chile's Atacama Desert is one of the driest places on Earth.
Easter Island belongs to Peru.
statements.truth: Easter Island, also called Rapa Nui, is part of Chile.

statements.text: Canada has the longest coastline of any country.
English and French are both official languages of Canada's federal government.
Most Canadians live in the country's far north.
statements.truth: Most Canadians live in the south, many of them fairly close to the border with the United States.

statements.text: India has the largest population of any country.
Chess is widely believed to come from an ancient Indian game called chaturanga.
Hindi is India's only official language.
statements.truth: Hindi and English are both official languages of the central government, and the constitution recognises 22 scheduled languages.

statements.text: Morocco's al-Qarawiyyin, founded in 859, is often called the oldest place of learning still in use.
At the Strait of Gibraltar, Morocco is only about 14 km (9 mi) from Spain.
Morocco's capital is Marrakesh.
statements.truth: Morocco's capital is Rabat. Casablanca is the biggest city, and Marrakesh is a famous historic city.

statements.text: Lake Baikal, in Siberia, is the deepest lake in the world.
The Trans-Siberian Railway is the longest railway line in the world.
At their closest point, Russia and the United States are more than 1,000 km apart.
statements.truth: In the Bering Strait, Russia's Big Diomede Island and the United States' Little Diomede Island are less than 4 km (2.5 mi) apart.

statements.text: Madagascar is the fourth-largest island in the world.
Wild lemurs live naturally only on Madagascar and a few small nearby islands.
Madagascar broke away from South America millions of years ago.
statements.truth: Madagascar separated from mainland Africa, and later from India, many millions of years ago.

statements.text: Two independent countries lie entirely inside Italy: San Marino and Vatican City.
The Po is Italy's longest river.
Pizza Margherita was named after a famous opera singer.
statements.truth: The usual story is that it was named after Queen Margherita of Savoy, who visited Naples in 1889.

statements.text: Indonesia is made up of more than 13,000 islands.
Komodo dragons, the world's largest lizards, live in the wild only in Indonesia.
Most Indonesians live on the island of Borneo.
statements.truth: More than half of Indonesians live on Java, one of the most densely populated islands on Earth.

statements.text: Ethiopia uses its own calendar, which runs about seven to eight years behind the Gregorian calendar.
The coffee plant is believed to have come originally from Ethiopia.
Ethiopia has a long coastline on the Red Sea.
statements.truth: Ethiopia has been landlocked since Eritrea became independent in 1993.

statements.text: Mexico City is built on the bed of a former lake, Lake Texcoco.
Mexico officially recognises 68 Indigenous languages.
Mexico's official name is the Republic of Mexico.
statements.truth: Mexico's official name is the United Mexican States (Estados Unidos Mexicanos).

statements.text: Finland has roughly 188,000 lakes.
Finnish isn't related to most European languages. One of its closest relatives is Estonian.
The sauna was invented in Sweden.
statements.truth: "Sauna" is a Finnish word, and Finnish sauna culture is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.

statements.text: The Great Barrier Reef, off Australia's northeast coast, is the world's largest coral reef system.
Canberra was built as Australia's capital partly as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.
Australia has more people than California.
statements.truth: Australia has about 28 million people. California alone has about 39 million.

statements.text: Machu Picchu was built by the Inca in the 1400s.
Lake Titicaca, on Peru's border with Bolivia, is often called the highest navigable lake in the world.
Peru's currency is the peso.
statements.truth: Peru's currency is the sol.

statements.text: Istanbul stretches across two continents, Europe and Asia.
Saint Nicholas, who inspired the legend of Santa Claus, was born in what is now Türkiye.
Istanbul is the capital of Türkiye.
statements.truth: The capital is Ankara. Istanbul is the largest city.

statements.text: In 1893, New Zealand became the first self-governing country to let women vote in national elections.
New Zealand has no native land snakes.
The kiwi, New Zealand's national bird, can fly short distances.
statements.truth: Kiwi are flightless. Their wings are tiny and hidden under their feathers.

statements.text: Mongolia is the most sparsely populated independent country in the world.
The Mongol Empire, founded by Genghis Khan, became the largest connected land empire in history.
Mongolia has a coastline on the Pacific Ocean.
statements.truth: Mongolia is landlocked, sitting between Russia and China.

statements.text: Greece has around 6,000 islands and islets, but only about 227 are inhabited.
The marathon race is named after Marathon, a town in Greece.
The ancient Olympic Games were held in Athens.
statements.truth: The ancient Games were held at Olympia, in the western Peloponnese. Athens hosted the first modern Games in 1896.

statements.text: Vietnam is one of the world's biggest coffee exporters.
Hạ Long Bay is dotted with around 1,600 limestone islands and islets.
Ho Chi Minh City is Vietnam's capital.
statements.truth: The capital is Hanoi, in the north. Ho Chi Minh City is the largest city.

statements.text: South Africa has 12 official languages.
South Africa has three capital cities: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.
Table Mountain overlooks Johannesburg.
statements.truth: Table Mountain overlooks Cape Town, more than 1,200 km (750 mi) from Johannesburg.

statements.text: Argentina is the eighth-largest country in the world by area.
Aconcagua, in Argentina, is the highest mountain outside Asia.
The tango was born in Brazil.
statements.truth: The tango grew up in the late 1800s around the Río de la Plata, in Buenos Aires and Montevideo.

statements.text: Switzerland has four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh.
Bern is officially called Switzerland's "federal city" rather than its capital.
The Matterhorn is Switzerland's highest mountain.
statements.truth: Switzerland's highest peak is the Dufourspitze, at 4,634 m. The Matterhorn is 4,478 m.

statements.text: Sri Lanka's tea is still sold as 'Ceylon tea', after the island's old name.
Sigiriya in Sri Lanka is an ancient rock fortress on top of a rock about 180 m (590 ft) high.
True cinnamon originally comes from South America.
statements.truth: True cinnamon, also called Ceylon cinnamon, is native to Sri Lanka.

statements.text: Vienna's Tiergarten Schönbrunn, opened in 1752, is the oldest zoo still running in the world.
Austria's Eisriesenwelt is the largest ice cave in the world.
Vienna's famous Sachertorte is a lemon sponge cake.
statements.truth: The Sachertorte is a chocolate sponge cake with apricot jam and a chocolate glaze, credited to Vienna's Franz Sacher.

statements.text: Haiti shares the Caribbean island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic.
French and Haitian Creole are the two official languages of Haiti.
Haiti is in the South Pacific Ocean, not far from Fiji.
statements.truth: Haiti is in the Caribbean Sea, on the western side of the island of Hispaniola.

statements.text: Togo is an island nation in the Indian Ocean, off the coast of East Africa.
statements.truth: Togo is on the West African mainland, between Ghana and Benin.

statements.text: French is the official language of Togo.
Togo's capital, Lomé, sits on the coast of the Gulf of Guinea.
Zambia's capital city is Lusaka.
Victoria Falls, one of the world's most famous waterfalls, sits on the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe.
Zambia has a long coastline on the Indian Ocean with sandy beaches.
statements.truth: Zambia is a landlocked country in Southern Africa with no coastline.

statements.text: The desert planet Tatooine in the first Star Wars film was filmed in Tunisia.
The ancient city of Carthage stood on the shore of the Lake of Tunis, in what is now Tunisia.
Tunisia's capital, Tunis, was named after the country.
statements.truth: It is the other way round: Tunisia is named after its capital city, Tunis.

statements.text: Sweden's Icehotel in Jukkasjärvi is rebuilt from ice and snow every winter.
Sweden's 'allemansrätten', or everyman's right, lets people hike across and even camp for a night or two on other people's land.
All the Nobel Prizes are awarded in Stockholm.
statements.truth: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway.

statements.text: Venezuela's Angel Falls is the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall.
Near Venezuela's Lake Maracaibo, the Catatumbo lightning storms flash on 140 to 160 nights a year.
The name Venezuela means 'Little Spain'.
statements.truth: Venezuela means 'Little Venice'. Explorers were reminded of Venice by houses built on stilts over the water.

statements.text: Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country in the world.
Vostok 1, which carried Yuri Gagarin into space, was launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.
The wild ancestor of the apple comes from the hills of Spain.
statements.truth: The main wild ancestor of today's apple, Malus sieversii, grows in the mountains of Central Asia, including Kazakhstan.

statements.text: Lesotho has long sandy beaches along the Indian Ocean.
statements.truth: Lesotho is landlocked and completely surrounded by South Africa.

statements.text: Lesotho is a kingdom, and its capital city is Maseru.
Lesotho is a very mountainous country in southern Africa.
Portuguese is the official language of Angola.
Angola is a country in South America, right next to Brazil.
statements.truth: Angola is in Southern Africa, across the Atlantic Ocean from Brazil.

statements.text: Angola has a long coastline on the Atlantic Ocean.
The United States bought Alaska from Russia in 1867.
Yellowstone, established in 1872, is considered the first national park in the world.
The Statue of Liberty was designed by an American sculptor.
statements.truth: The Statue of Liberty was designed by French sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi and was a gift from France.

statements.text: The shore of the Dead Sea, on Jordan's western border, is the lowest land on Earth.
Petra's famous buildings are carved directly into pinkish sandstone cliffs.
Jordan has no coastline at all.
statements.truth: Jordan has a short coastline on the Gulf of Aqaba, at its port city of Aqaba.

statements.text: The cravat, ancestor of the necktie, became fashionable in France in the 1660s thanks to the knotted neck scarves of Croatian soldiers.
Croatia has more than 1,000 islands and islets along its Adriatic coast.
The Dalmatian dog breed is named after a region of Hungary.
statements.truth: The Dalmatian is named after Dalmatia, a region of Croatia on the Adriatic coast.

statements.text: Burkina Faso is a coastal country in East Africa with beaches on the Indian Ocean.
statements.truth: Burkina Faso is a landlocked country in West Africa.

statements.text: The capital and largest city of Burkina Faso is Ouagadougou.
Burkina Faso shares a border with Ghana to the south.
Spain's national anthem, the Marcha Real, has no official lyrics.
At La Tomatina, a festival in the town of Buñol, people throw tomatoes at each other.
The Sagrada Família in Barcelona was completed in 1926.
statements.truth: Construction began in 1882 and has gone on for well over a century. Gaudí died in 1926 with the church far from finished.

statements.text: Lake Malawi, a huge lake, runs along most of Malawi's eastern border.
Malawi is an island nation in the Caribbean Sea.
statements.truth: Malawi is a landlocked country in southeast Africa.

statements.text: Malawi is nicknamed "the Warm Heart of Africa" for its friendly people.
Colombia's Caño Cristales is nicknamed the 'river of five colours'.
Colombia has coastlines on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.
Colombia is named after its first president.
statements.truth: Colombia is named after Christopher Columbus.

statements.text: Eswatini is a small kingdom in Southern Africa.
Eswatini is almost completely surrounded by South Africa, with Mozambique on its eastern side.
Eswatini is famous for its long sandy beaches on the Atlantic Ocean.
statements.truth: Eswatini is landlocked, so it has no coastline at all.

statements.text: Oman is located on the Arabian Peninsula in West Asia.
Oman's capital city is Dubai.
statements.truth: Oman's capital is Muscat. Dubai is a city in the United Arab Emirates.

statements.text: Arabic is the official language of Oman.
The Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa.
The Gambia is surrounded by Senegal on every side except its Atlantic coast.
Spanish is the official language of The Gambia.
statements.truth: English is the official language of The Gambia.

statements.text: Bengali, also called Bangla, is the official language of Bangladesh.
The Bengal tiger is the national animal of Bangladesh.
Bangladesh is almost entirely surrounded by China.
statements.truth: Bangladesh is almost entirely surrounded by India, with a short border with Myanmar.

statements.text: Paraguay is a landlocked country in the middle of South America.
Paraguay has two official languages: Spanish and Guaraní.
Paraguay's capital city is Buenos Aires.
statements.truth: Paraguay's capital is Asunción. Buenos Aires is the capital of Argentina.

statements.text: Zimbabwe has a long coastline on the Atlantic Ocean.
statements.truth: Zimbabwe is landlocked and has no coastline at all.

statements.text: The famous Victoria Falls waterfall is shared by Zimbabwe and Zambia.
Harare is the capital and largest city of Zimbabwe.
San Marino is a small, flat island in the middle of the Mediterranean Sea.
statements.truth: San Marino is landlocked, perched on Monte Titano and completely surrounded by Italy.

statements.text: San Marino is a tiny country completely surrounded by Italy.
Italian is the official language of San Marino.
A gold harp on a blue background is Ireland's coat of arms.
Newgrange, a passage tomb in Ireland built around 3100 BC, is older than Stonehenge and the Egyptian pyramids.
Halloween grew out of an old Irish festival called Beltane.
statements.truth: Halloween's roots lie in Samhain, a Gaelic festival marking the end of the harvest. Beltane is a spring festival.

statements.text: Liberia is a country in South America, next to Brazil.
statements.truth: Liberia is in West Africa, on the Atlantic coast.

statements.text: Liberia's capital and largest city is Monrovia.
English is the official language of Liberia.
Djibouti is a small country in the Horn of Africa.
Djibouti is landlocked, with no access to the sea.
statements.truth: Djibouti has a coastline on the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.

statements.text: French and Arabic are the two official languages of Djibouti.
Armenia's capital city is Yerevan.
Armenia has a long, sunny coastline on the Black Sea.
statements.truth: Armenia is a landlocked country in the South Caucasus.

statements.text: The Armenian language is written in its own unique alphabet.
Antigua and Barbuda is an island country in the Caribbean.
Antigua and Barbuda is an island nation in the Pacific Ocean, near Fiji.
statements.truth: Antigua and Barbuda is in the Caribbean.

statements.text: The country is named after its two main islands, Antigua and Barbuda.
The saxophone was invented by Belgian instrument maker Adolphe Sax.
Belgium has three official languages: Dutch, French and German.
Brussels' famous Manneken Pis statue is more than 10 m (33 ft) tall.
statements.truth: The Manneken Pis is tiny, only about 55.5 cm (22 in) tall.

statements.text: Most people in Honduras speak Portuguese.
statements.truth: Spanish is the official language of Honduras, spoken by almost everyone.

statements.text: Honduras is in Central America and has a coastline on the Caribbean Sea.
The ancient Maya city of Copán is found in Honduras.
São Tomé and Príncipe is an island country in the Gulf of Guinea, off Central Africa.
Portuguese is the official language of São Tomé and Príncipe.
São Tomé and Príncipe is a landlocked country in the middle of the Sahara Desert.
statements.truth: São Tomé and Príncipe is made up of islands in the Gulf of Guinea.

statements.text: Timor-Leste is a country in Southeast Asia that shares the island of Timor with Indonesia.
Timor-Leste's two official languages are Portuguese and Tetum.
Timor-Leste is a landlocked country with no coastline.
statements.truth: Timor-Leste is an island country covering the eastern half of the island of Timor.

statements.text: The DR Congo is named after the mighty Congo River, which flows through it.
Kinshasa is the capital and largest city of the DR Congo.
The DR Congo is a small island nation in the Indian Ocean.
statements.truth: The DR Congo is a huge country in Central Africa, the second-largest in Africa.

statements.text: Lake Volta in Ghana is one of the largest artificial lakes in the world by surface area.
On 6 March 1957, Ghana became the first colony in sub-Saharan Africa to gain independence.
Kente cloth comes originally from Kenya.
statements.truth: Kente is a woven cloth from Ghana, made by the Akan and Ewe peoples.

statements.text: Benin is in East Africa, sharing a border with Kenya.
statements.truth: Benin is in West Africa, between Togo and Nigeria.

statements.text: French is the official language of Benin.
Benin's neighbours include Togo to the west and Nigeria to the east.
Liechtenstein has sunny beaches along the Mediterranean Sea.
statements.truth: Liechtenstein is a landlocked country in the Alps between Switzerland and Austria.

statements.text: The capital of Liechtenstein is Vaduz.
German is the official language of Liechtenstein.
The Dominican Republic shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti.
Most people in the Dominican Republic speak French.
statements.truth: The Dominican Republic is mostly Spanish-speaking.

statements.text: Baseball is by far the most popular sport in the Dominican Republic.
Georgia's capital city is Tbilisi.
Georgia is home to some of the world's earliest known winemaking sites.
The country of Georgia is landlocked, with no sea coast.
statements.truth: Georgia lies on the east coast of the Black Sea.

statements.text: The capital of Seychelles is Victoria.
Seychelles is a group of islands in the Caribbean Sea.
statements.truth: Seychelles is a group of islands in the Indian Ocean, east of Africa.

statements.text: Huge numbers of giant tortoises live on Aldabra, an atoll in Seychelles.
The Lut Desert in Iran has recorded some of the hottest ground temperatures on Earth, up to 70.7 °C (159 °F).
Qanats, underground channels that carry water from hills to farms, were developed in ancient Iran.
Persian, Iran's main language, is a form of Arabic.
statements.truth: Persian is an Indo-European language, though it is written in a script based on Arabic.

statements.text: Belize is an island nation in the Mediterranean Sea.
statements.truth: Belize is in Central America, on the coast of the Caribbean Sea.

statements.text: English is the official language of Belize.
Belize is famous for its huge barrier reef in the Caribbean Sea.
Malta's Ġgantija temples, on the island of Gozo, are older than the pyramids of Egypt.
Maltese grew out of Sicilian Arabic but is written in the Latin alphabet.
Malta is made up of a single island.
statements.truth: Malta is an archipelago. Its three main islands are Malta, Gozo and Comino.

statements.text: Rwanda is a landlocked country in East Africa.
Rwanda is a vast, flat desert country in North Africa.
statements.truth: Rwanda is a small, hilly country in East Africa, nicknamed the land of a thousand hills.

statements.text: Rwanda's Volcanoes National Park is a famous home of mountain gorillas.
Bhutan sits in the Himalayas, between China and India.
Bhutan's capital and largest city is Thimphu.
Ice hockey is Bhutan's national sport.
statements.truth: Archery is the national sport of Bhutan.

statements.text: Botswana is home to the Okavango Delta, a vast inland river delta.
Botswana is a landlocked country in southern Africa.
Nairobi is the capital of Botswana.
statements.truth: Gaborone is the capital of Botswana; Nairobi is the capital of Kenya.

statements.text: Saint Lucia is an island country in the eastern Caribbean Sea.
The Pitons, two steep volcanic peaks, are Saint Lucia's most famous landmark.
Saint Lucia is a Pacific island country located next to Fiji.
statements.truth: Saint Lucia is in the eastern Caribbean Sea, part of the West Indies.

statements.text: The official language of Mozambique is French.
statements.truth: Portuguese is the official language of Mozambique.

statements.text: Mozambique is in Southeast Africa, with the Indian Ocean along its eastern coast.
Maputo is the capital and largest city of Mozambique.
Skopje is the capital and largest city of North Macedonia.
North Macedonia is in Scandinavia, right next to Sweden.
statements.truth: North Macedonia is a landlocked country in southeastern Europe, in the Balkans.

statements.text: Lake Ohrid lies on North Macedonia's border with Albania.
Zuma Rock, a huge natural monolith in Nigeria, appears on the 100-naira banknote.
More than 500 native languages are spoken in Nigeria.
Lagos is Nigeria's capital.
statements.truth: Abuja has been Nigeria's capital since 1991. Lagos is its biggest city.

statements.text: The Philippines is made up of more than 7,600 islands.
The Chocolate Hills on Bohol are more than 1,000 grassy, cone-shaped hills that turn brown in the dry season.
The Philippines is named after a Spanish explorer.
statements.truth: The Philippines is named after King Philip II of Spain.

statements.text: Uganda has a long coastline on the Indian Ocean.
statements.truth: Uganda is landlocked, though it shares the huge Lake Victoria with Kenya and Tanzania.

statements.text: Uganda's capital city is Kampala.
English and Swahili are the official languages of Uganda.
Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is an island country in the eastern Caribbean.
The capital of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is Havana.
statements.truth: The capital is Kingstown. Havana is the capital of Cuba.

statements.text: English is the official language of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.
The Rubik's Cube was invented in 1974 by Hungarian architect Ernő Rubik.
Hungary's Lake Hévíz is the largest thermal lake in Europe that people can swim in.
Hungarian is closely related to German.
statements.truth: Hungarian is a Uralic language, distantly related to Finnish and Estonian.

statements.text: Moldova has many sandy beaches on the Black Sea.
statements.truth: Moldova is landlocked, sitting between Romania and Ukraine.

statements.text: Moldova is well known for making and exporting wine.
Chișinău is the capital and largest city of Moldova.
Trinidad and Tobago is a Caribbean country just off the coast of Venezuela.
The main official language of Trinidad and Tobago is Portuguese.
statements.truth: English is the official language of Trinidad and Tobago.

statements.text: Trinidad and Tobago is the birthplace of the steelpan, a drum made from steel.
Gabon is on the Atlantic coast of Central Africa, and the equator runs through it.
Libreville is the capital and largest city of Gabon.
Spanish is the official language of Gabon.
statements.truth: French is the official language of Gabon.

statements.text: Andorra sits high in the Pyrenees mountains, between France and Spain.
Catalan is the official language of Andorra.
Andorra is one of the biggest countries in Europe.
statements.truth: Andorra is a tiny microstate, one of the smallest countries in Europe.

statements.text: Qatar's only land border is with Saudi Arabia.
Khor Al Adaid in Qatar is an 'inland sea' where the Persian Gulf reaches deep into the desert.
Qatar is an island in the Persian Gulf.
statements.truth: Qatar is a peninsula that juts out from the Arabian Peninsula into the Persian Gulf.

statements.text: Saint Kitts and Nevis is made up of two islands in the Caribbean.
English is the official language of Saint Kitts and Nevis.
Saint Kitts and Nevis is one of the biggest countries in the Americas.
statements.truth: Saint Kitts and Nevis is the smallest sovereign country in the Western Hemisphere.

statements.text: English is the official language of the Republic of the Congo.
statements.truth: French is the official language of the Republic of the Congo.

statements.text: The capital and largest city of the Republic of the Congo is Brazzaville.
The Republic of the Congo is in Central Africa and lies on the equator.
Slovakia is a landlocked country in Central Europe.
Prague is the capital of Slovakia.
statements.truth: Bratislava is the capital of Slovakia; Prague is the capital of the Czech Republic.

statements.text: The Tatra Mountains rise in the north of Slovakia.
The capital of Laos is Vientiane.
Laos has long sandy beaches along the Indian Ocean.
statements.truth: Laos is the only landlocked country in Southeast Asia.

statements.text: Sticky rice is a staple food in Laos.
Marie Curie, the first person to win two Nobel Prizes, was born in Warsaw.
Poland's Wieliczka Salt Mine has underground chapels and statues carved by miners out of rock salt.
Poland's Białowieża Forest is home to Europe's last wild tigers.
statements.truth: Białowieża Forest is famous for its European bison, Europe's heaviest land animal.

statements.text: Bulgaria is a country in Southeastern Europe, on the Balkan Peninsula.
Bulgaria's capital city is Bucharest.
statements.truth: Bulgaria's capital is Sofia. Bucharest is the capital of Romania.

statements.text: Bulgaria has a coastline on the Black Sea.
Romania's Palace of the Parliament in Bucharest is described as the world's heaviest administrative building.
Romanian is a Romance language, descended from Latin.
Most of the Danube Delta lies in Bulgaria.
statements.truth: Most of the Danube Delta lies in Romania, with a small part in Ukraine.

statements.text: Ecuador's name is simply the Spanish word for 'equator'.
Because Earth bulges at the equator, the summit of Ecuador's Chimborazo is the farthest point from Earth's centre.
Panama hats were first made in Panama.
statements.truth: Panama hats come from Ecuador. Many were shipped through Panama on their way to buyers abroad.

statements.text: Mauritius is a landlocked country in central Africa.
statements.truth: Mauritius is an island country in the Indian Ocean, east of Madagascar.

statements.text: The dodo, a famous flightless bird, once lived only on Mauritius.
Port Louis is the capital and largest city of Mauritius.
Singapore is made up of one main island and more than 60 smaller islands and islets.
The name Singapore goes back to a Sanskrit word meaning 'Lion City'.
Singapore lies more than 1,000 km (620 mi) north of the equator.
statements.truth: Singapore is only about 137 km (85 mi) north of the equator.

statements.text: Big Ben is the nickname of the great bell in London's clock tower, not the tower itself.
The London Underground began in 1863 with the world's first underground passenger railway.
Stonehenge was built by the Romans.
statements.truth: Stonehenge was built in prehistoric times, roughly 3000 to 2000 BC, thousands of years before the Romans arrived.

statements.text: Most people in Uzbekistan speak Hindi as their main language.
statements.truth: Uzbek, a Turkic language, is the official language of Uzbekistan.

statements.text: Uzbekistan is a country in Central Asia.
The Registan, a grand square lined with three madrasas, is a famous landmark in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.
Mali is a country in West Africa.
The historic city of Timbuktu, once a famous centre of learning, is in Mali.
Mali is a chain of tropical islands in the Indian Ocean.
statements.truth: Mali is a landlocked country in West Africa. The island nation is the Maldives.

statements.text: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world by area.
The Pontifical Swiss Guard has protected the popes since 1506.
Vatican City has its own airport.
statements.truth: Vatican City has no airport, though it does have a heliport and a short railway.

statements.text: Nicaragua is the largest country in Central America by area.
Spanish is the official language of Nicaragua.
Nicaragua is located in Southeast Asia.
